description: Cost of living breakdowns for Indonesian provinces/cities, compiled from BPS (Badan Pusat Statistik) poverty-line and CPI data, Kemnaker's official KHL (Kebutuhan Hidup Layak) standard, and Numbeo crowdsourced price data. Intended as a companion to a separate file of UMP/UMK minimum wages and average/median wages by province, so wages can be compared against actual living costs. As of the 2026-09-03 update, the file's headline addition is 'itemized_cost_of_living_by_city' - a genuinely itemized per-category (housing, food, transportation, utilities, entertainment/leisure, childcare/education, clothing) cost breakdown for 16 Indonesian cities, pulled from Numbeo's full cost-of-living tables rather than just rent/groceries/utilities totals.
sources: https://databoks.katadata.co.id (various per-province 'Garis Kemiskinan Makanan dan Nonmakanan' articles, individually cited per row below, all attributing BPS as the underlying source)
https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/ (per-city pages, individually cited per row below)

https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/in/<City> and https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/in/<City>-Indonesia (per-city itemized pages, individually cited per row in itemized_cost_of_living_by_city below - 16 cities successfully retrieved: Jakarta, Surabaya, Bandung, Yogyakarta, Semarang, Medan, Makassar, Denpasar, Palembang, Malang, Tangerang, Bogor, Batam, Balikpapan, Pekanbaru, Padang)

https://www.biem.co/read/2021/04/27/77903/64-komponen-kebutuhan-hidup-layak/ and https://luk.staff.ugm.ac.id/atur/tk/Permennakertrans13-2012KebutuhanHidupLayak.pdf (national standard KHL component-category structure, no province-level rupiah values)

https://www.cnbcindonesia.com/news/20251218112834-4-695350/ini-10-daerah-dengan-kebutuhan-hidup-layak-tertinggi-di-indonesia (checked in this session - confirms all top-10 KHL figures reported nationally are province-level, not kabupaten/kota)
notes: This file layers four fundamentally different, non-interchangeable data types and none should be treated as a single authoritative 'cost of living index': (1) poverty_line_by_province is BPS's official Garis Kemiskinan (GK) — a per-capita subsistence-level monthly expenditure threshold used to define poverty, NOT a typical household budget; it is the most consistent, officially structured province-level series and is the backbone of this file. (2) cpi_by_city is BPS's Consumer Price Index / inflation data by expenditure group — this turned out to be the weakest-covered section: BPS publishes full IHK-by-group tables by city (see 'Indeks Harga Konsumen 150 Kabupaten/Kota di Indonesia 2025' publication cited above), but that table lives in a PDF/JS-rendered publication that automated web tools could not extract cell-by-cell in this session, so only partial, mostly headline/'biggest mover' figures could be retrieved for a handful of cities plus the national aggregate — this section should be treated as illustrative only, not a substitute for pulling the BPS publication directly. (3) numbeo_cost_breakdown_by_city gives absolute IDR figures (rent, food, transport, utilities) but is explicitly CROWDSOURCED/user-submitted, self-selected toward expat and urban-middle-class respondents, and can be sparse or volatile, especially outside Java/Bali. (4) khl_breakdown_by_region is Kemnaker's official 2025/2026 Kebutuhan Hidup Layak figure — the decent-living-needs benchmark wage councils use as an input to minimum-wage decisions — but despite searching, this session could not locate a publicly available province-by-province breakdown into the individual KHL components (makanan/minuman, sandang, perumahan, pendidikan, kesehatan, transportasi, rekreasi/tabungan, etc.); only the official TOTAL KHL per province could be sourced with confidence, so 'components' is null throughout that section and should not be assumed to exist elsewhere — it would need to come from the underlying regional wage-council survey reports (Dewan Pengupahan), which are scattered, non-digitized, and locality-specific. IMPORTANT DATA QUALITY CAVEAT on poverty_line_by_province: for many provinces, the food + non-food component figures extracted from source pages did NOT arithmetically sum to the stated total garis kemiskinan (the source pages present multi-year time series and the mismatch likely reflects the extraction tool picking food/non-food figures from a different period row than the total, or true urban/rural sub-splits being conflated with the provincial total). Rather than fabricate a reconciled split, rows where food+non-food did not sum to within rounding of the stated total have food_poverty_line and non_food_poverty_line set to null, with only the total (which is corroborated by the article title/headline and is the figure BPS itself publishes as the primary series) retained; this is flagged per-row via 'component_reconciliation'. Also note many databoks articles are labeled 'Desember' for a March/September BPS round — BPS's poverty line is only measured in March and September; where source text muddled these, the period given here follows the article's own explicit month/year label, which may not perfectly align with BPS's official March/September release calendar. Coverage gaps: poverty_line_by_province has no data at all for Aceh, Riau (mainland), Sumatera Selatan, and Papua Selatan despite searching (KHL totals for these ARE available). cpi_by_city and numbeo tables cover only a handful of major cities, not the ~90 BPS-monitored cities or all 38 provincial capitals. Do not treat any figure here as a live/current price — always re-verify against the cited source before using for decisions. UPDATE 2026-09-03: (5) A new 'itemized_cost_of_living_by_city' section was added, giving a genuinely itemized per-category breakdown (housing/rent+buy, food/groceries+restaurants, transportation, utilities, entertainment/leisure, childcare/education, clothing) for 16 cities, all sourced from Numbeo's full cost-of-living tables (not just the 3-4 fields the old numbeo_cost_breakdown_by_city section had) - see that section's own long caveat note for sample-size, unit, and currency-display details; treat it as the most complete but still crowdsourced/self-selected section in this file. Two cities explicitly requested (Bekasi, Depok) have NO dedicated Numbeo cost-of-living page at all (only a paywalled estimator) and were therefore omitted rather than padded with nulls. cpi_by_city gained two cities (Kolaka, DI Yogyakarta) with COMPLETE 11-expenditure-group breakdowns, but six other cities tried in this session (Medan, Palembang, Surabaya, Bandung, Kendari, Kudus) still could not be extracted because their BPS pages render the group table via JavaScript or bundle it only in a PDF - this remains the file's weakest section overall. khl_breakdown_by_region's per-province 'components' fields are STILL null after a renewed, more targeted search in this session - genuinely could not be found publicly for any individual province in the current round - but a new 'khl_standard_component_categories' field now documents the official national ~60-64 item component STRUCTURE (item names, no rupiah) that every provincial survey is required to follow, which at least clarifies what a real component breakdown would look like if one is later located. UPDATE 2026-09-03 (kabupaten/kota granularity pass): (6) poverty_line_by_province was RENAMED to 'poverty_line_by_region' and now holds BOTH province-level rows (unchanged from before, each tagged "level": "province") AND ~514 new kabupaten/kota-level rows (tagged "level": "kabupaten/kota") sourced from BPS's official annual publication 'Data dan Informasi Kemiskinan Kabupaten/Kota Tahun 2025' (Table 2.1, garis kemiskinan rupiah/kapita/bulan) - this is a real, distinct, officially published BPS dataset (not an extrapolation from the province-level Garis Kemiskinan series), obtained via a GoodStats-hosted PDF mirror since bps.go.id's own page for this table, and every provincial/kabupaten BPS subdomain's equivalent 'statistics-table' page, render the data as a JavaScript widget that this session's web-fetch tool could not extract (the same failure mode already documented for cpi_by_city above). Coverage: all 38 provinces have at least some kabupaten/kota rows, most provinces have their FULL kabupaten/kota roster (e.g. all 27 Jawa Barat, all 35 Jawa Tengah, all 38 Jawa Timur, all 8 Banten, all 5 DI Yogyakarta, all 9 Bali, all 33 Sumatera Utara, and so on for the remaining provinces) - this was a single AI-driven PDF-table extraction pass, not hand-verified row-by-row against the source PDF's page images, so treat individual values as high-confidence (official BPS figures) but not manually cross-checked; food/non-food component sub-splits were NOT available at kabupaten/kota granularity in the extracted table (only the total), so those two fields are null on every new kab/kota row, mirroring how many of the pre-existing province rows already had to leave that split null. Kabupaten/kota rows appear to be a period close to the province rows' 'March 2025' figures (aggregating a kab/kota province's rows by simple population-weighted-style average lands close to the already-published province total in every spot-checked case, e.g. Jawa Barat's 18+9=27 rows average to essentially the province's 547,750 figure, DI Yogyakarta's 5 rows to essentially 626,360) but the exact official reference period for Table 2.1 was not restated by the GoodStats mirror text, so 'period' on these rows is labeled accordingly as an approximation rather than a confirmed exact month. (7) khl_breakdown_by_region entries (all still province-level, Kemnaker 2025/2026 totals) were each tagged "level": "province" for filtering purposes, and ONE genuine kabupaten/kota-level KHL figure was added and tagged "level": "kabupaten/kota": Kabupaten Boyolali (Jawa Tengah), Rp3,321,012, from a KSPN-conducted regional wage-council-adjacent survey reported by local news (Espos.id) for the UMK 2026 proposal round - flagged as a single/lajang-worker figure, methodologically not guaranteed comparable to the province KHL totals nearby. See 'kabupaten_kota_khl_coverage_note_2026_09_03' for why broader kabupaten/kota KHL coverage was NOT achievable in this session despite a renewed, targeted search across Jawa Barat, Jawa Tengah, Jawa Timur, Banten, DI Yogyakarta, Bali, and Sumatera Utara (the provinces this update explicitly prioritized, per the OTHER companion file umr_umk_2026.json's full kab/kota UMK rosters for those provinces) - unlike poverty line, KHL genuinely has no single indexed public dataset compiling kabupaten/kota-level rupiah figures; each region's Dewan Pengupahan Daerah conducts and reports its own survey independently, mostly as one-off local news mentions (often only as vague union claims of what KHL 'should' be, not the wage council's own official survey result) rather than structured, aggregatable data, so kabupaten/kota-level KHL coverage in this file remains extremely thin (1 of roughly 500+ regions) and should NOT be read as representative - the honest state of public data on this specific indicator, not a search-effort shortfall.

cpi_by_city_coverage_note: This section improved somewhat in this session (added Kolaka and DI Yogyakarta, both with COMPLETE 11-group breakdowns pulled from static BPS press-release pages) but is still the weakest in the file overall. BPS DOES publish full IHK-by-expenditure-group tables for ~90-150 monitored cities (see 'Indeks Harga Konsumen 150 Kabupaten/Kota di Indonesia 2025 (2022=100)' at bps.go.id/id/publication), but most individual per-city BPS pages (e.g. medankota.bps.go.id, sumsel.bps.go.id for Palembang, surabayakota.bps.go.id, bandungkota.bps.go.id, sultra.bps.go.id for Kendari, kuduskab.bps.go.id) render their category tables via JavaScript/interactive widgets or bundle them only inside a downloadable PDF 'Berita Resmi Statistik', neither of which this session's web-fetch tool could extract cell-by-cell - repeated attempts against six additional cities in this session all failed for that reason (confirmed via direct fetch, not assumed). The pattern that DID work: smaller/regional BPS offices (Kolaka) and DIY's provincial release happened to render their group table as plain HTML text rather than a JS widget. Anyone needing full city-level CPI-by-group data for cities not covered above should pull the BPS 'Indeks Harga Konsumen 150 Kabupaten/Kota' publication directly, or the city's own BRS PDF, rather than relying on this section.

itemized_cost_of_living_by_city_note: New section added 2026-09-03, superseding numbeo_cost_breakdown_by_city above as the primary Numbeo-derived source in this file (that section is kept only for backward compatibility/history and several of its rows are now stale relative to this one - e.g. the retry on Denpasar succeeded this time). This pulls Numbeo's full per-category table (Restaurants, Markets, Transportation, Utilities, Sports And Leisure, Childcare, Clothing And Shoes, Rent, Buy Apartment) for every Indonesian city this session could successfully load a dedicated cost-of-living page for. IMPORTANT CAVEATS: (1) All figures are CROWDSOURCED/user-submitted to Numbeo, not an official survey - sample sizes range from Jakarta/Surabaya (hundreds of entries, tens of contributors) down to Padang (9 entries from 3 contributors) and Palembang (24 entries from 1 contributor); treat small-sample cities as illustrative/order-of-magnitude only, not precise. (2) Numbeo's own per-city pages do NOT display an explicit 'USD to IDR exchange rate used' - prices are shown natively in IDR (Numbeo lets the viewer pick display currency; these pages were fetched with IDR as the shown currency), so no independent USD->IDR conversion was applied here; figures are Numbeo's own IDR-denominated crowdsourced entries, not a currency conversion by this session. (3) 'as_of' below is Numbeo's own stated 'last update' date/contributor-window for that city's page (varies city to city, from Nov 2025 to Sept 2026), NOT a single consistent survey date across cities - do not treat this as a single point-in-time cross-city snapshot. (4) Grocery/market item units follow Numbeo's own units verbatim (mostly pounds (lb) and 50oz/12oz bottles, NOT kg/500g/1.5L as a idealized schema might assume) - converting would risk silent errors, so unit is stated in each key name. (5) buy_price_per_sqm_* fields are DERIVED by this session (Numbeo publishes price-per-square-foot; multiplied by 10.7639 sq ft/sq m and rounded) - not a Numbeo-native figure, flagged via 'buy_price_derived_from_per_sqft'. (6) Bekasi and Depok were explicitly requested but Numbeo has NO dedicated cost-of-living data page for either (confirmed via direct URL attempts and web search - only a paywalled 'Cost of Living Estimator' input form and city-comparison utility exist, no priced data table); they are omitted from this section rather than padded with nulls. Makassar, Medan, Bogor, Pekanbaru, Balikpapan, Palembang, Padang, and Batam all required a '-Indonesia' URL suffix (e.g. /cost-of-living/in/Makassar-Indonesia) to resolve - the plain city-name URL 404'd for these even though it worked for Jakarta/Surabaya/Bandung/etc.

khl_breakdown_components_search_note_202: This session made a renewed, harder attempt to find province-level itemized KHL rupiah breakdowns (per the specific search strategies suggested: 'rincian KHL [provinsi] [tahun]', Dewan Pengupahan/disnaker reports, news itemizing the 7-group KHL survey). Result: STILL could not locate any publicly indexed source giving actual rupiah values per KHL component group (makanan/minuman, sandang, perumahan, pendidikan, kesehatan, transportasi, rekreasi & tabungan) for ANY individual province in the current 2025/2026 KHL round - all 'components' fields below remain null for that reason, honestly, rather than fabricated. What WAS newly found and added (see 'khl_standard_component_categories' below) is the underlying NATIONAL STANDARD component structure that every provincial/kabupaten KHL survey is required to follow under Permenakertrans No. 13/2012 (as amended) - i.e. the ~60-64 item list and which of the 7 main groups each item belongs to, WITHOUT rupiah values, since those are set locally by each Dewan Pengupahan Daerah (regional wage council) via its own market survey and are not centrally published/digitized anywhere this session could reach. Provincial/kabupaten disnaker offices and Dewan Pengupahan Daerah reports (which DO contain the priced component tables) appear to exist only as internal survey documents, local news mentions of the TOTAL figure only, or PDFs not indexed/crawlable by the search and fetch tools available in this session - obtaining real per-component rupiah splits would likely require directly contacting a specific province's Dewan Pengupahan or disnaker office, or the BPS/Kemnaker microdata underlying the survey, rather than public web search.

khl_standard_component_categories.description: The official national KHL component structure (not province-specific rupiah values - see khl_breakdown_components_search_note_2026_09_03 above) that Kemnaker's Permenakertrans No. 13/2012 (as revised) requires every regional KHL survey to itemize. Each region's Dewan Pengupahan Daerah prices these same ~60 items locally each year to produce that region's total_khl figure in khl_breakdown_by_region above; only the item LIST is standardized nationally, the prices are not.

kabupaten_kota_khl_coverage_note_2026_09: This session made a renewed, harder attempt (per explicit instruction) to find kabupaten/kota-level KHL rupiah figures for Jawa Barat, Jawa Tengah, Jawa Timur, Banten, DI Yogyakarta, Bali, and Sumatera Utara specifically - the provinces with full UMK kab/kota rosters in the companion umr_umk_2026.json file - using search patterns for 'hasil survei KHL [kabupaten/kota] [tahun]', provincial disnaker/Dewan Pengupahan press releases, and 'UMK vs KHL' comparison articles that sometimes surface such tables for UMP (province) purposes. Result: national/province-level KHL round-ups (Kemnaker's Dec 2025 release, CNBC Indonesia's 'top 10 highest KHL' piece, GoodStats' '38 provinces' piece) all confirmed to be PROVINCE level only when checked directly. Individual regency/city news searches surfaced plenty of articles about UMK PROPOSALS being 'below KHL' (Pandeglang, Lebak, Sukoharjo, etc.) but these almost always quote a labor union's informal claim of what KHL 'should be' rather than a citable rupiah figure from the region's own Dewan Pengupahan survey - the sole exception found was Kabupaten Boyolali (Jawa Tengah), now included above. This matches the structural reality described in the task itself: KHL surveys ARE conducted per kabupaten/kota by each local Dewan Pengupahan, but unlike BPS's poverty line (which BPS itself compiles and publishes nationally every year in one document, table 2.1 of 'Data dan Informasi Kemiskinan Kabupaten/Kota'), no equivalent central compiler exists for KHL - each region's survey result lives only in that region's own disnaker/Dewan Pengupahan paperwork, which is largely undigitized, unindexed, and not consistently reported by local media in rupiah-figure form. Obtaining broader kabupaten/kota KHL coverage would most likely require directly requesting survey results from each province's Dinas Tenaga Kerja / Dewan Pengupahan Daerah, not further public web search.
